text:
Samir: FYI I pushed profiling data from the nightly that started failing 08:00 UTC. Perf regression looks correlated with the new kernel-routing patch + smaller block allocator defaults. attaching quick notes and a flame snippet.

Jia: link? can you paste the top hotspots, or a short flame please?

Samir: pasted below (TL;DR): generic_attention_kernel jumped from 6% -> 28% of GPU time for long sequences; allocator spent ~40ms extra per batch due to increased compaction churn. Flame: 
```
generic_attention_kernel 28%
kv_cache_copy 12%
block_manager::compact_range 9%
workspace_alloc(align) 6%
batch_router::select_kernel 4%
```

Mateo: wait - generic kernel increased because route chose smaller-block-friendly kernels but the workspace estimator still told runtime to reserve big contiguous workspace, so it falls back to generic?

Samir: exactly. New block size (48k -> microblock) reduces average waste and improves reuse in steady-state, but transient requests cause more compaction calls. The kernel selector then sometimes picks "optimized_block_kernel" which expects contiguous workspace; when alloc fails we catch and fallback to generic. That fallback cost is what spiked.

Lena: what does the batching histogram look like? Are we seeing more cross-batch fragmentation when many short and a few long requests interleave?

Samir: yes. Batching heatmap: most batches are short (<=128) but tail of ~2% are long (>1024). Those long ones trigger large KV growth and force block splits. When long arrives into an active microblock pool it forces compaction and slow path.

Kai: ops-bot reported two OOMs during the run? ops-bot: "oom-detected: gpu0 workspace_alloc failed at 1849876556, falling back to slow kernel"

Jia: possible mitigations: (1) dynamic workspace estimator that consults max_seq_in_batch rather than global reserved size; (2) optimistic kernel routing with a quick try/catch and immediate revert to previous kernel without full compaction; (3) temporarily increase microblock spare pool for tail-heavy hours. Thoughts?

Mateo: I prototyped (1) yesterday. Using per-batch workspace_hint reduced fallback rates by 70% in microbench. The estimator uses max(seq_lengths) * per_token_workspace + small_slack. cheap to compute.

Lena: for (2) we need metrics: how often does fallback cost exceed just running generic from start? If fallback cost > 2x generic, prefer pessimistic routing. We should add "fallback_latency" meter.

Samir: agreed. Proposed action plan:
- revert allocator default block_limit -> keep current microblock_size at 64k today to stop damage (short-term revert).
- enable per-batch workspace estimator behind feature flag and run A/B for 24h.
- add fallback_latency metric + sample traces for fallbacks.
- tune compaction: avoid full-range compaction when workload is taily, instead prefer targeted eviction of least-recently-used microblocks.

Jia: +1. Can we ship the estimator as a safe opt-in in the next patch? I'll own rollout. Also add logs: "batch_ws_hint=%d kernel_choice=%s fallback=%b" to help analysis.

Mateo: I'll open a small PR with the estimator and unit tests. Will include perf microbench results (reduction in fallback_count and avg_alloc_latency).

Kai: I've scheduled a quick rollback window at 09:30 UTC if A/B shows any user-facing increase. ops-bot logged the schedule.

Lena: one more ask — include a short experiment that increases microblock spare pool by +20% and measure compaction_count. If that reduces compaction without too much memory waste it's a viable stopgap.

Samir: noted. I'll attach the full flame + raw heap traces in the issue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-rollback-window scheduled by Kai at 2025-11-13T09:30:00Z

Jia: leaving checklist here:
- [ ] revert default microblock_size (Samir)
- [ ] feature-flag per-batch-ws-estimator (Jia)
- [ ] add fallback_latency metric (Lena)
- [ ] microblock-spare +20% experiment (Mateo)
- [ ] collect 24h A/B data and run statistical test (Jia/Mateo)

Mateo: starting PR now, will ping when CI green.

Samir: ping me once PR lands; I'll attach traces and approve quick rollback if anything noisy shows up.
